title: Camel and Horse Rides at Giza: Welfare and What to Know
excerpt: Camel and horse rides at the Giza pyramids: how to agree a price before you mount, the welfare checks that matter, and what is changing on the plateau.
body_html:
Prices, timetables and visiting details are a November 2026 snapshot. Check the linked official pages and your departure’s current inclusions and terms before booking.

The quick answer

Ride a camel at Giza only if the animal looks healthy and the price is agreed before you mount. Rides are arranged privately with handlers on the spot and paid in Egyptian pounds; Sawa Tours does not sell or arrange them, and they are never part of a Sawa tour price. There is no official tariff, and tips and photo fees are where disputes start. Reports in 2026 say Egypt is restricting camel and horse rides around the pyramids in favour of electric shuttles, but no official end date has been published and licensed handlers still operate, so skipping the ride is easier every year.

UNESCO describes the pyramid fields from Giza to Dahshur as one World Heritage site.

Key facts

Fact Detail (as of November 2026)
Where The panorama area and desert edge of the Giza plateau, on the western side of Greater Cairo
Options A camel photo stop, a short loop, a longer desert viewpoint trip; a horse photo or ride
Cost Negotiated in Egyptian pounds, in cash, on site. No official price list exists
Included in Sawa tours No. Sawa does not sell or arrange rides, and the Giza tour pages list camel rides as not included
Golden rule Agree the total price, for the whole party and the return trip, before mounting
Plateau entry for context EGP 700 (about €12 at EGP 60 to the euro, 8 November 2026) for a foreign adult, EGP 350 for a student; gates from 7:00, last entry 16:00 (Ministry ticketing portal)
Welfare status Welfare groups have documented overwork and mistreatment. Reports from July 2026 say rides are being restricted in favour of electric shuttles; guides say handlers are now licensed and limited to set zones. No official end date has been confirmed
Best time Morning: cooler and kinder for travellers and animals alike
See Giza on Sawa Giza Pyramids, Sphinx & the Grand Egyptian Museum, from €71 · Giza Uncovered: Pyramids, Sphinx & Stories, from €29 (per person, as listed in November 2026)

Few Giza questions divide travellers like the camel ride. Some dream of the panorama photo from camel-back; others have heard the scam stories or the welfare concerns and want nothing to do with it. Both instincts are sensible. This post covers how to agree a fair price before anyone mounts, how to judge the animal, and a balanced look at the animal-welfare concerns now reshaping the plateau. Sawa Tours (sawa.tours) is a shared-departure marketplace for Egyptian day tours and short tours; its founder, Islam Hussein, has worked in Egyptian tourism since 1993.

Camel and horse rides at Giza: the short answer

A camel or horse ride at the Giza pyramids is optional, arranged on site and paid in cash. Handlers offer photo stops and short rides on dromedaries (the one-humped camels of Egypt) around the panorama viewpoint. Treat it as a small private deal: agree the price first, check the animal, and walk away freely if either is not right.

What do camel and horse rides cost at Giza?

Nobody publishes an official tariff, so the honest answer is a method rather than a number. Rides are negotiated in Egyptian pounds, first quotes are often well above what people end up paying, and traveller accounts published in 2026 describe the same few disputes again and again:

  • Photos. Extra charges for photos, revealed at dismount. Agree whether photos are included.
  • Currency. A price agreed in one currency and then claimed in another. Agree the currency as well as the number.
  • Per person or per animal. Quotes are often per person for one direction, so the return can cost extra. Ask for the total for your whole party and the return.

For context, the plateau entry ticket is EGP 700 for a foreign adult, bought separately from any ride. Ride money is paid in cash to the handler.

How to agree a fair price before you mount

Agree everything before a hand touches the saddle. That single habit prevents most Giza ride disputes:

  1. Fix the total in Egyptian pounds. For your whole party, for the return trip. Repeat it back, which kills the "per person" and "one-way" surprises.
  2. Set the duration and route aloud. "Ten minutes, around the panorama and back" beats an "over there" argued about later.
  3. Ask whether photos are included. If the answer is vague, treat it as no.
  4. Bargain politely. Haggling is expected; settle where both sides are comfortable. Opening near half the first quote is a common approach, not a rule.
  5. Carry small notes. Exact change closes the deal; a large note invites a change-making dance.
  6. Decide any tip in advance. It is appreciated, never mandatory; hand it to the handler yourself.

The one non-negotiable: total price, in Egyptian pounds, for the whole party and the return trip, agreed before you mount. Everything after that is flexible.

The animal welfare concerns at Giza, honestly

The concerns are real and have been documented by animal-welfare groups. PETA's investigation alleged overwork, harsh handling and animals worked to death, and in early 2025 Airbnb and several other travel companies stopped selling tours and experiences that include camel and horse rides at the pyramids. Those are advocacy-group claims and company decisions; they are not an official finding. Many handlers care well for the animals that support their families, but the pattern was serious enough that the site itself is changing.

What is reported about the change is less solid than it sounds. In July 2026 several outlets reported that Egypt "has moved to restrict" camel and horse rides around the pyramids and replace them with electric buses and carts, but those reports rely largely on social media posts and cite no named official or date. Separately, PETA said the Ministry of Tourism had announced plans to end rides at Giza as long ago as 2020. What visitors can see is this: a new main entrance at the Pyramids Visitor Centre, a free electric shuttle included with admission, private cars and tour buses kept off the plateau, and, according to recent guides, camel and horse handlers licensed and limited to specific zones. As of November 2026 rides can still be bought, so the change looks gradual rather than a finished ban.

How to choose a responsible option (or skip the ride)

If you want the ride, spend two minutes choosing the animal as carefully as the price:

  • Bright eyes, even gait. No limping, no visible wounds or saddle sores, ribs not sharply showing.
  • Water and shade nearby. A handler resting beside a full trough is telling you something good.
  • Calm handling, no whipping. A healthy animal does not need it, and you should not pay for it.
  • A visible licence. Recent guides advise choosing a handler who can show one.
  • Short and cool. Morning rides are kinder; midday plateau heat is brutal on two legs and four.

And skipping is always easy: "la, shukran" (no, thank you) works, and the free electric shuttle makes the car-free panorama simple.

The verdict on camel rides at Giza

A camel ride at Giza is a fair pleasure if you treat it as a negotiation and a welfare check at once: agree the total in EGP before mounting, look the animal over, keep it short in the heat. faq.q: Should I ride a camel at the Pyramids?
faq.a: Only if the animal looks healthy and the price is agreed before you mount; otherwise enjoy the plateau on foot. Many travellers find a short, fairly paid loop near the panorama a genuine highlight, and others skip it without regret. Neither choice is wrong, and the free electric shuttle makes the no-ride option easy.

faq.q: Are camel rides included in Sawa tour prices?
faq.a: No. Sawa does not sell or arrange rides, and the Giza tour pages list camel rides as not included. If you choose to ride, it is a private deal with the handler, paid in cash on site.

faq.q: Is it safe to ride a camel at Giza?
faq.a: For most travellers, yes, with basic care. Getting on and off are the wobbly moments, so keep both hands free, wear long trousers and let the handler settle the camel before you climb. Camels stand and kneel in stages, so stay seated while they do. Keep rides short in summer heat, and have a child ride with an adult beside them.

faq.q: Why is Egypt restricting camel and horse rides at Giza?
faq.a: For animal-welfare and site-modernisation reasons: the plateau has faced years of documented concern about working animals, and 2026 reports say authorities are moving towards electric buses and carts. The reports are based mainly on social media and name no official or end date, so rides may still be offered during your visit.

faq.q: What happens if my Sawa departure never fills?
faq.a: Nothing is charged. A date confirms when four travellers have reserved it, and until then no card is involved. If it has not reached four seven days before the tour, it is cancelled, Sawa suggests another date and you have paid nothing. Once confirmed, a date is not cancelled for low numbers, and the price stays fixed per traveller with no solo surcharge.
